vision.oneLine: Group accounting: decide what kind of investee you have (subsidiary, joint operation, joint venture, associate), then consolidate it line by line, take your share of its assets, or equity-account it.
vision.why: The single most-tested area of FR: long consolidated balance sheet practicals, control assessments, NCI changes, loss of control and equity-method MCQs appear in nearly every paper, RTP and MTP from 2022 to 2026.
vision.marks: about 12–16 marks an attempt (often one full practical)

items: Joint control → joint operation or joint venture

sixty: Control = power + variable returns + link; only substantive rights count.
Consolidate from the date control is obtained until it is lost.
Goodwill = consideration + NCI + old stake − net assets (all fair value).
Eliminate intra-group items 100%; upstream unrealised profit is shared with NCI.
Stake changes while in control → equity; no goodwill change.
Losing control → derecognise everything, fair-value what is kept, gain to P&L.
Joint operation: your assets and liabilities; joint venture: equity method.
Associate: 20% presumption; equity method; eliminate only your share of upstream/downstream profit.

askedAs.how: Consolidated balance sheet with fair-value adjustments, NCI, pre/post-acquisition split and intra-group items.
Does X control Y? Joint operation or joint venture? Associate or not?
NCI after a stake change, gain on loss of control, equity-method carrying amount.

pitfalls: Eliminating only the parent's share of unrealised intra-group profit for a subsidiary.
Taking the gain on a stake sale without loss of control to P&L.
Not fair-valuing the retained interest on loss of control.
Treating a protective right as giving power.
Using proportionate consolidation for a joint venture.
Eliminating 100% of profit on sales to an associate.

levels.title: Control: power, returns, link
levels.hook: Every group question begins with "does X control Y?"

teach.html: Power over relevant activities, exposure to variable returns, ability to use power to affect returns.
Only substantive rights; protective rights never give power.
Contracts with other vote holders, other contractual rights, de facto control (size vs dispersion), substantive potential voting rights.

recall.q: A lender's right to seize assets on default gives it power.
Option to buy 40% more (from 30%) exercisable within 25 days; next decision meeting in 30 days. The option is…
recall.why: Exercisable before decisions are needed (SM Example 3).

recall.q: Investor 30% + fellow subsidiary 30% acting as its de facto agent. Votes the investor can direct (%)?

levels.title: Principal or agent; investment entities
levels.hook: Fund-manager control questions and investment-entity exemptions recur in RTPs.

teach.html: Narrow authority, a single party able to remove without cause, commensurate arm's-length fee, small other interests.
Investment management for investors, invests solely for returns, fair-value management. Measures subsidiaries at FVTPL; its non-investment-entity parent consolidates all.

recall.q: A single investor who can remove the fund manager without cause makes the manager an agent.
An investment entity consolidates a subsidiary that provides investment-related services and is not itself an investment entity.
A parent of an investment entity that is not itself an investment entity…
opts: Consolidates all entities it controls, including through the investment entity

twist.q: The fund manager also holds 35% of the fund and fees rise with profits?
twist.a: Greater variability of returns → likely principal → consolidate.

levels.title: Consolidation procedure: goodwill, NCI, policies, dates, eliminations
levels.hook: The marks in a 16-mark practical sit in these workings.

teach.html: Goodwill working at fair values; NCI at fair value or proportionate share.
Uniform policies, same date (gap ≤ 3 months), depreciation on fair values, 100% elimination of intra-group items, NCI share of profit even if NCI goes negative.

recall.q: Reporting-date gap allowed under Ind AS 110 (months)?
Profit ₹5,00,000; NCI holds 10% cumulative preference ₹10,00,000; parent 80%. Parent's share (₹)?
Unrealised profit on goods sold by a 60% subsidiary to the parent is eliminated only to 60%.
recall.why: Eliminated in full; NCI bears 40% because it is upstream.

twist.q: The parent sold the goods to the subsidiary instead?
twist.a: Downstream: still eliminate in full, but the parent bears it all — NCI unaffected.

levels.title: Changes in stake and loss of control
levels.hook: Almost every recent MTP has one: B96 equity entry or a loss-of-control gain.

teach.html: Equity transaction: adjust NCI; the difference to other equity; goodwill unchanged; no P&L.
Derecognise assets, goodwill, liabilities, NCI; recognise consideration and retained stake at fair value; reclassify OCI; gain to P&L.

recall.q: Buy 10% more of a 70% subsidiary for ₹2,600 thousand; NCI (30%) ₹6,600 thousand. Debit to other equity (₹ thousand)?
Goodwill is reduced when the parent sells 10% of a subsidiary but keeps control.
Sell 50% of a 60% subsidiary, keep 10% (FV ₹1,00,000). The retained 10% is recorded at…

twist.q: The 10% retained still gives board representation and significant influence?
twist.a: The ₹1,00,000 becomes the cost of an associate under Ind AS 28.

levels.title: Chain holdings
levels.hook: Effective-interest percentages decide NCI in sub-subsidiaries.

teach.html: Group % = product down the chain + direct holdings; NCI = the rest.
Pre-acquisition reserves depend on whether the parent bought the subsidiary before or after the subsidiary bought the sub-subsidiary.

recall.q: P 80% of S1, S1 60% of S2. Group interest in S2 (%)?
P 80% of S1, S1 75% of S2, P 10% direct. Group interest (%)?
S2 is not a subsidiary of P because the group owns only 48%.

twist.q: S1 bought S2 after P bought S1?
twist.a: S2 comes under control when S1 acquires it; pre-acquisition reserves are at that later date.

levels.title: Joint arrangements
levels.hook: Classification (JO vs JV) is a frequent descriptive question.

teach.html: Contract + unanimous consent of the parties sharing control over relevant activities.
No separate vehicle → JO. Vehicle: legal form, contract terms, other facts (output to parties + parties fund it → JO).
JO: own assets, liabilities, revenue, expenses (gains on contributions only to others' share). JV: equity method.

recall.q: A joint venture is proportionately consolidated under Ind AS.
Separate company, but the two parties take all output and fund all its cash needs. Type?
Decisions need any 75% of votes, achievable by different combinations of three parties. Joint control exists.
recall.why: Unless the contract specifies which parties must agree.

twist.q: Unanimity is required only for changes to the constitution and new share issues?
twist.a: Protective rights only — no joint control.

levels.title: Associates and the equity method
levels.hook: Equity-method carrying amounts and upstream/downstream eliminations are standard MCQs.

teach.html: 20% presumption; board seat, policy participation, material transactions, managers, technical information.
Cost + share of profit (fair-value adjusted) + share of OCI − dividends; goodwill inside; eliminate only investor's share of upstream/downstream profit.
Stop at zero (including long-term interests); fair-value a retained financial asset; associate ↔ JV no remeasurement.

recall.q: Holding presumed to give significant influence (%)?
An associate becoming a joint venture is remeasured to fair value.
A Ltd 15%, its subsidiary 10%, its JV 10% in X Ltd. Interest for the equity method?
recall.why: Ignore holdings of the JV (SM Example 2).

twist.q: The associate's losses exceed the equity investment but A holds a long-term loan to it?
twist.a: Continue absorbing losses against the loan (after Ind AS 109), in reverse order of seniority.

compare.title: Subsidiary vs joint venture vs associate

rows.b: Inside the carrying amount; whole investment tested

sorter.s: Profit on sales to the investee is eliminated only to the investor's share.
Measured at cost or Ind AS 109 in separate statements.
Recognised at fair value on initial recognition as a financial asset.
sorter.why: That is an Ind AS 109 investment, neither.
